intent.raw_query: Mexico City food and culture, $900 solo, 5 days, any month 2026

experiences.name: Mercado de San Juan Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore one of Mexico City's most iconic gourmet markets, sampling exotic cheeses, fresh seafood tostadas, traditional tamales, and regional delicacies from across Mexico. Chat with local vendors and discover ingredients used in authentic Mexican cuisine.

experiences.name: Museo Nacional de Antropología Visit
experiences.description: Spend a half-day at one of the world's greatest museums, exploring ancient Aztec, Maya, and Olmec artifacts including the famous Aztec Sun Stone. The museum offers deep insight into Mexico's pre-Hispanic civilizations and indigenous cultures.

experiences.name: Street Taco Crawl in Coyoacán
experiences.description: Wander through the bohemian neighborhood of Coyoacán stopping at legendary taco stands for al pastor, carnitas, and barbacoa tacos. Visit the colorful Mercado de Coyoacán for fresh tlayudas and aguas frescas while soaking in the artistic local atmosphere.

experiences.name: Frida Kahlo Museum (La Casa Azul)
experiences.description: Tour the iconic Blue House where Frida Kahlo was born and lived, now a museum showcasing her personal belongings, artwork, and the vibrant cultural world she inhabited. A deeply moving cultural experience that connects art, identity, and Mexican history.

experiences.name: Mezcal Tasting and Traditional Dinner in Roma Norte
experiences.description: Join a guided mezcal tasting session at a local cantina learning about the artisanal production process, followed by a traditional Mexican dinner featuring mole negro, chiles en nogada, and handmade tortillas at a neighborhood fondita beloved by locals.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Mexico City
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Mexico City International Airport at 22:30. Clear customs and immigration, then take the Metro Line 5 (Terminal Aérea station) or an authorized airport taxi to reach Aegean Bliss Resort. Keep your luggage secure and exchange a small amount of currency at the airport if needed. Check in, freshen up, and rest.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport before departure
meals.lunch: On the plane or at the airport
meals.dinner: Grab a quick late-night bite near the hotel — look for a 24-hour OXXO convenience store or a nearby taquería open late for budget tacos (50–80 MXN)

day_by_day.notes: Keep taxi costs low by using the official airport taxi booths (pre-paid, ~350–450 MXN) or Metro (~5 MXN). Avoid unlicensed taxis. Have your hotel address written down in Spanish.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recover from travel. After a leisurely start, head to the historic Centro Histórico. Visit the massive Zócalo (Plaza de la Constitución), one of the largest city squares in the world — free entry. Walk to the stunning Catedral Metropolitana (free to enter) and admire its baroque architecture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Templo Mayor archaeological site (entry ~80 MXN), the ruins of the ancient Aztec temple at the heart of old Tenochtitlán. Afterward, stroll through the surrounding streets of Centro Histórico, browse street vendors, and visit the Palacio Nacional to see Diego Rivera's famous murals — free entry.
day_by_day.evening: Walk along Avenida Francisco I. Madero, a pedestrian street full of local life and street performers. Visit the Casa de los Azulejos (House of Tiles), a stunning 18th-century building — free to admire from outside. Wind down with a walk around the lit-up Zócalo at night.

meals.breakfast: Eat at the hotel or find a local mercado nearby — chilaquiles or tamales from a market stall (40–70 MXN)
meals.lunch: Mercado de San Juan or a comida corrida (set lunch menu) at a local fondita near Centro — soup, main dish, and drink for ~80–120 MXN
meals.dinner: Tacos at a street taquería near Centro Histórico — try tacos de canasta or al pastor (15–25 MXN each, budget 60–100 MXN total)

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes. Centro Histórico is very walkable. Keep an eye on your belongings in crowded areas. Metro is the cheapest transport (~5 MXN per ride).

day_by_day.morning: Visit Chapultepec Park, one of the largest urban parks in the world — free entry. Stroll through the park, enjoy the lake, and visit the free sections including the botanical garden. Hike up to Chapultepec Castle (entry ~85 MXN) for panoramic views of the city and exhibits on Mexican history.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Museo Nacional de Antropología (National Museum of Anthropology), one of the finest museums in the world — entry ~85 MXN. Spend 2–3 hours exploring pre-Hispanic artifacts including the famous Aztec Sun Stone. Afterward, walk through the Condesa or Roma neighborhood to soak in the bohemian, tree-lined streets and colorful architecture.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Colonia Roma — browse local shops, street art, and plazas. Visit Parque México, a charming neighborhood park popular with locals. Enjoy the vibrant evening atmosphere of this trendy but accessible neighborhood.

meals.breakfast: Grab fresh fruit, juice, and a torta from a street cart near Chapultepec (~50–80 MXN)
meals.lunch: Eat at a comida corrida restaurant in Colonia Roma — a full set meal with agua fresca for ~100–130 MXN
meals.dinner: Try a local tostada or tlayuda spot in Roma or Condesa — budget around 80–120 MXN for a satisfying meal

day_by_day.notes: Chapultepec is free on Sundays for Mexican citizens; foreigners may still pay. Museo de Antropología is closed on Mondays. Metro Line 1 (Chapultepec station) gives easy access.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to Xochimilco, famous for its ancient canal system and colorful trajineras (gondola-style boats). Hire a shared trajinera with other tourists (100–150 MXN per person for a shared ride) and float through the canals lined with floating gardens (chinampas). This is a UNESCO World Heritage site and a deeply local cultural experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Mercado de Xochimilco for incredibly cheap and authentic local food — try tlayudas, elotes (grilled corn), and fresh-squeezed juice. Return to the city center and visit Coyoacán, the charming colonial neighborhood. Walk through its cobblestone streets and visit the Jardín Centenario and Jardín Hidalgo plazas — free.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the Museo Frida Kahlo (La Casa Azul / Blue House) — entry ~270 MXN, book online in advance as it sells out. Explore the colorful streets of Coyoacán at dusk, browse artisan markets, and enjoy the lively local atmosphere around the main plaza.

meals.breakfast: Eat at the hotel or grab a quick torta and atole from a street stall before heading out (~50–70 MXN)
meals.lunch: Lunch at Mercado de Xochimilco — fresh, authentic, and very cheap (60–100 MXN for a full meal)
meals.dinner: Try a local restaurant in Coyoacán — enchiladas, mole, or pozole at a neighborhood fondita (100–150 MXN)

day_by_day.notes: Xochimilco is about 1 hour from the city center by Metro + bus or pesero (minibus). Take Metro Line 2 to Tasqueña, then the tren ligero to Xochimilco (~10 MXN total). Book Frida Kahlo Museum tickets online well in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Mercado de la Merced or Mercado de Medellín — two of Mexico City's most vibrant and authentic local markets. Browse fresh produce, spices, street food, and handmade goods. This is a fantastic cultural immersion and very budget-friendly. Try a traditional Mexican breakfast at a market stall.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Barrio de Tepito street market area (stay alert and go earlier in the day) or visit the Mercado de Artesanías (craft market) near the Ciudadela — great for picking up affordable souvenirs like textiles, pottery, and folk art. Visit the nearby Biblioteca de México (free) and the surrounding Colonia Centro streets.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Centro Histórico for a final evening stroll. Visit the rooftop bar of a budget hotel near Zócalo for a drink with a view (many offer affordable beers ~60–80 MXN). Watch the sunset over the historic district. Pack and prepare for departure or continued travel.

meals.breakfast: Full traditional breakfast at Mercado de la Merced — huevos rancheros, fresh juice, and café de olla (40–70 MXN)
meals.lunch: Comida corrida at a local fondita near La Ciudadela — 3-course set menu with drink (~100–120 MXN)
meals.dinner: Final dinner at a beloved local taquería — splurge slightly on tacos de barbacoa or carnitas with all the fixings (~100–150 MXN)

day_by_day.notes: Keep receipts and budget tracker handy for the trip. Daily budget estimate: 400–700 MXN (~$20–35 USD) per day covering food, transport, and entry fees. Mexico City Metro is your best friend for cheap, fast transit across the city.

trip_options.title: Classic Mexico City Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Aeropuerto Internacional Benito Juárez at 22:30. Take an authorized airport taxi or pre-booked ride service to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and get settled into your room.

meals.dinner: Grab a late-night snack at a 24-hour taqueria near the hotel or order room service if available. Try tacos de canasta or quesadillas for a quick, affordable, and authentic first taste of Mexico City.

day_by_day.notes: Flight arrives late — keep Day 1 light. Download maps offline and exchange some currency at the airport for convenience. Rest well for a full Day 2 ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Start with a leisurely breakfast, then head to the Historic Center (Centro Histórico). Visit the Zócalo, one of the largest city squares in the world. Explore the stunning Metropolitan Cathedral and walk around the Templo Mayor archaeological site — an ancient Aztec temple with an excellent on-site museum.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to the Palacio Nacional to see Diego Rivera's famous murals depicting Mexican history. Then stroll through the nearby Mercado de la Merced or Mercado Abelardo Rodríguez to soak in local market culture — vendors selling fresh produce, spices, and street food. Browse artisan crafts and souvenirs at mid-range prices.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Alameda Central park for a relaxing evening stroll. Explore the surrounding streets and visit the Palacio de Bellas Artes to admire its stunning Art Nouveau exterior illuminated at night.

meals.breakfast: Café El Popular near the Zócalo — a beloved local institution open early. Try chilaquiles or tamales with café de olla (around $5–8 USD).
meals.lunch: El Cardenal, a classic mid-range restaurant near the Historic Center serving traditional Mexican cuisine. Try sopa azteca and mole dishes (around $12–18 USD per person).
meals.dinner: Los Girasoles near Alameda Central — a well-regarded restaurant offering traditional Mexican dishes with a modern twist at mid-range prices (around $15–20 USD per person).

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes — the Historic Center involves a lot of walking on cobblestones. Most museums are free or low-cost on Sundays. Watch your belongings in crowded market areas.

day_by_day.morning: Take a morning trip to Xochimilco, a UNESCO World Heritage Site famous for its ancient canal system. Rent a colorful trajinera (flat-bottomed boat) for a 2-hour ride through the canals. Enjoy the festive atmosphere with floating flower vendors and local musicians.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the nearby Museo Frida Kahlo (La Casa Azul) in Coyoacán — the iconic blue house where Frida Kahlo was born and lived. Afterward, explore the charming Coyoacán neighborhood: browse the artisan market, visit the central plaza, and enjoy the bohemian local vibe.
day_by_day.evening: Spend the evening in Coyoacán, one of Mexico City's most atmospheric neighborhoods. Enjoy the lively plaza, street performers, and browse local art galleries.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or a nearby café before heading out early to Xochimilco.
meals.lunch: Eat on the trajinera! Buy fresh food from floating vendors on the canals — grilled corn (elote), tamales, and fresh fruit are budget-friendly and delicious (around $5–10 USD total).
meals.dinner: Corazón de Maguey in Coyoacán — a fantastic mid-range restaurant specializing in traditional Oaxacan cuisine and mezcal. Try the tlayudas and mole negro (around $15–20 USD per person).

day_by_day.notes: Book Frida Kahlo Museum tickets in advance online — it sells out frequently. Arrive at Xochimilco early (before 11am) to avoid weekend crowds. Trajinera rental costs approximately $20–30 USD for a small group for 2 hours.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Teotihuacán, the ancient pre-Columbian city located about 50km northeast of Mexico City. Climb the Pyramid of the Sun and Pyramid of the Moon for breathtaking panoramic views. Walk the Avenue of the Dead and explore the Temple of Quetzalcoatl. This is one of the most impressive archaeological sites in the Americas.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Mexico City and head to the trendy Condesa or Roma neighborhood. Stroll through Parque México, a beautiful Art Deco park surrounded by elegant architecture. Browse independent boutiques, bookshops, and galleries along Amsterdam Avenue and Álvaro Obregón.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Roma Norte neighborhood's vibrant dining and nightlife scene. Visit a mezcalería for a guided tasting of traditional Mexican spirits.

meals.breakfast: Grab an early breakfast before departure — street tacos or tortas from a market stand near the hotel (around $3–5 USD).
meals.lunch: Eat at the Teotihuacán site — there are several mid-range restaurants near the ruins. La Gruta, a restaurant set inside a natural cave near the pyramids, offers a unique dining experience with traditional Mexican dishes (around $12–18 USD per person).
meals.dinner: Contramar in Colonia Roma — a legendary seafood restaurant beloved by locals and visitors alike. Known for their tuna tostadas and grilled fish (around $18–25 USD per person). Reserve ahead.

day_by_day.notes: Take an early bus or organized tour to Teotihuacán (buses depart from Terminal Central del Norte). Wear sunscreen and a hat — the archaeological site has very little shade. Carry water. The site opens at 9am; aim to arrive early before midday heat and crowds.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the world-class Museo Nacional de Antropología (National Museum of Anthropology) in Chapultepec — one of the greatest museums in Latin America, housing extraordinary collections of Aztec, Maya, and other pre-Columbian artifacts including the famous Aztec Sun Stone.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stroll through Bosque de Chapultepec, Mexico City's expansive urban park. Visit Chapultepec Castle (Castillo de Chapultepec) perched on a hill with sweeping city views and fascinating exhibits on Mexican history. Wind down with a relaxing walk through the park's tree-lined paths.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Polanco, Mexico City's upscale neighborhood, for a final evening of dining and exploration. Browse the elegant Presidente Masaryk avenue and enjoy a farewell dinner celebrating your trip.

meals.breakfast: Café Nin in Colonia Juárez — a stylish, mid-range café known for excellent coffee and creative breakfast dishes like avocado toast and egg dishes with Mexican flavors (around $8–12 USD).
meals.lunch: Lunch at the museum café inside the Museo Nacional de Antropología, or grab a casual bite from one of the food stands in Chapultepec park (around $5–10 USD).
meals.dinner: Pujol (splurge option) or Quintonil in Polanco for a special farewell dinner featuring innovative modern Mexican cuisine. If budget is a concern, try Mercado de Medellín for a more casual but equally delicious final meal with a wide variety of local dishes (Pujol: $50–80 USD per person; Mercado option: $8–15 USD).

day_by_day.notes: The Anthropology Museum is massive — allocate at least 3 hours. The museum is closed on Mondays, so this plan assumes Day 5 falls on a Wednesday. Chapultepec Castle and the museum are within walking distance of each other. Consider purchasing a combined ticket. Begin packing in the evening if departing the next day.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Mexico City Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: No morning activities — late arrival day
day_by_day.afternoon: No afternoon activities — late arrival day
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Mexico City International Airport at 22:30 on Flight UA. A private luxury transfer will whisk you to Aegean Bliss Resort. Upon check-in, enjoy a welcome amenity — chilled mezcal cocktail and seasonal fruit platter prepared by the resort. Take time to settle into your suite and unwind after the journey.

meals.dinner: Late-night in-room dining at the resort: order a curated selection of light Mexican bites such as tlayudas, guacamole with heirloom tortillas, and a glass of premium Oaxacan mezcal from the resort's private bar menu.

day_by_day.notes: Arrival is at 22:30, so no activities are scheduled before check-in. Confirm private airport transfer in advance with the resort concierge. Keep the first evening relaxed to adjust to local time. Mexico City sits at 2,240 meters altitude — stay hydrated and rest well.

day_by_day.morning: Begin your first full day with a leisurely breakfast at the resort, then embark on a private guided tour of the Historic Centro. Visit the magnificent Zócalo — one of the largest public squares in the world — followed by an exclusive behind-the-scenes tour of the Metropolitan Cathedral and the Templo Mayor archaeological site with a private archaeologist guide who will narrate the layered Aztec and colonial history in vivid detail.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the stunning Palacio de Bellas Artes for a curated private walkthrough of its iconic murals by Diego Rivera and José Clemente Orozco. Afterward, stroll through the charming streets of the Alameda Central area and visit the Museo Franz Mayer, a world-class decorative arts museum housed in a 16th-century hospital. A private docent will guide you through its extraordinary collection of colonial silver, textiles, and ceramics.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy sunset cocktails on a rooftop bar overlooking the Centro Histórico — Gran Hotel Ciudad de México's rooftop terrace is an iconic choice. Then proceed to dinner at Contramar or Pujol (reserve well in advance), two of Mexico City's most celebrated fine-dining restaurants offering elevated modern Mexican cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at the resort featuring Mexican staples — chilaquiles verdes, fresh tropical fruit, pan dulce, and artisan coffee from Veracruz.
meals.lunch: Lunch at El Cardenal in Centro Histórico — a legendary institution renowned for its traditional Mexican cuisine, including mole negro, tamales, and exceptional atole drinks.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Pujol — Chef Enrique Olvera's world-renowned restaurant offering a tasting menu that reinterprets Mexican culinary heritage with extraordinary finesse. Pair with a curated Mexican wine or mezcal flight.

day_by_day.notes: Book Pujol or Contramar weeks in advance — they are among the most sought-after reservations in Latin America. Private guided tours can be arranged through the resort concierge. Comfortable walking shoes recommended for Centro exploration.

day_by_day.morning: Depart early for the ancient pyramids of Teotihuacán, just 50 km northeast of the city, via private luxury vehicle. Arrive before the general public crowds for an exclusive early-access tour with a private archaeologist. Climb the Pyramid of the Sun and the Pyramid of the Moon and explore the Avenue of the Dead with expert commentary on this mysterious pre-Columbian metropolis.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the city and head to the bohemian neighborhood of Coyoacán — the birthplace of Frida Kahlo. Visit the Museo Frida Kahlo (Casa Azul) with a VIP reservation to avoid queues, exploring the artist's personal belongings, paintings, and lush gardens. Afterward, wander Coyoacán's cobblestone streets, browse artisan markets, and sip on tejate or horchata at a local café.
day_by_day.evening: Experience a private mezcal and tequila tasting masterclass hosted by a certified sommelier at a luxury mezcalería in Roma Norte or Condesa neighborhood. Cap the night with dinner at Quintonil, another globally ranked Mexico City restaurant celebrated for its hyper-local, seasonal tasting menus.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before departure — light options such as yogurt parfait, fresh juices, and avocado toast to prepare for the Teotihuacán climb.
meals.lunch: Picnic-style luxury lunch arranged by your private guide at Teotihuacán — gourmet boxes with artisan cheeses, charcuterie, fresh salsas, handmade tortillas, and agua fresca, enjoyed with a view of the pyramids.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Quintonil — Chef Jorge Vallejo's celebrated tasting menu showcasing Mexican ingredients in innovative, elegant preparations. Exceptional wine and cocktail pairing available.

day_by_day.notes: Teotihuacán early access (before 9 AM) is highly recommended to avoid crowds and midday heat. Wear sunscreen and bring a hat for the pyramid climb. The resort concierge can arrange a seamless private round-trip transfer. Quintonil reservations should be secured well in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Spend the morning in the elegant Polanco neighborhood — Mexico City's most upscale district. Visit the world-class Museo Soumaya, a striking silver-façaded building housing over 66,000 works of art including pieces by Rodin, Dalí, and Rivera. Afterward, explore the nearby Museo Jumex, a contemporary art museum with rotating exhibitions from leading international and Mexican artists.
day_by_day.afternoon: Indulge in a premium culinary experience: join a private market tour and hands-on cooking class led by a celebrated local chef. Visit Mercado de Medellín or Mercado de San Juan — Mexico City's gourmet market — to source exotic ingredients, taste artisan cheeses, chiles, and tropical fruits, then head to a private kitchen studio to prepare traditional dishes such as mole, ceviche, and chiles en nogada.
day_by_day.evening: Treat yourself to a world-class spa experience at the resort or a top luxury hotel spa in Polanco. Then enjoy a private rooftop dinner experience — arrange with the concierge for a bespoke candlelit dinner on a private terrace or rooftop with panoramic city views, curated by a personal chef with a multi-course tasting menu and sommelier-selected wine pairings.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Café Nin in Juárez neighborhood — a chic, design-forward café beloved for its elevated Mexican brunch dishes, including huevos divorciados, pan de cazón, and exceptional coffee.
meals.lunch: Enjoy the fruits of your cooking class as your midday meal — a multi-course lunch you prepared yourself with your private chef instructor, accompanied by agua fresca and local craft beer.
meals.dinner: Private bespoke rooftop dinner experience arranged by the resort concierge — a fully personalized multi-course Mexican tasting menu with wine pairing, under the stars with city views.

day_by_day.notes: The private cooking class should be arranged 2–3 days in advance through the concierge. Mercado de San Juan is particularly renowned for gourmet and imported products — an extraordinary cultural and culinary experience. The spa session should also be pre-booked.

day_by_day.morning: Start your final morning with a serene visit to the Floating Gardens of Xochimilco — a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Board a private, flower-adorned trajinera (flat-bottomed boat) for an exclusive guided tour of the ancient Aztec canals, complete with onboard breakfast, live marimba music, and a local naturalist guide explaining the history and ecology of this extraordinary waterway system.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the city for last-minute luxury shopping in Polanco along Presidente Masaryk Avenue — Mexico City's answer to the Champs-Élysées — featuring flagship stores of international and Mexican luxury brands. Visit Mercado Roma for artisan souvenirs, gourmet pantry items, and specialty mezcal to bring home. Stop by a high-end chocolatier such as Tout Chocolat for handcrafted Mexican chocolate gifts.
day_by_day.evening: Conclude your premium Mexico City journey with a farewell dinner at Máximo Bistrot — a beloved farm-to-table restaurant in Roma Norte celebrated for its seasonal, ingredient-driven menu and warm atmosphere. Raise a glass of fine Mexican wine or a perfectly crafted mezcal Negroni to an unforgettable trip. Return to the resort for a relaxed final night, with a late checkout arranged if needed.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet onboard breakfast on the trajinera at Xochimilco — fresh fruit, tamales, champurrado, and pan dulce served as you glide through the ancient canals.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Mercado Roma — a curated food hall in Roma Norte offering an array of premium stalls. Graze on oysters, gourmet tacos, artisan cheeses, and fresh ceviche at your leisure.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Máximo Bistrot — intimate, elegant, and ingredient-obsessed. The seasonal tasting menu reflects the best of what Mexican producers offer, paired with natural wines and exceptional service.

day_by_day.notes: Xochimilco is best visited on weekday mornings to avoid weekend crowds. Book the private trajinera through the concierge for the most exclusive experience. Confirm late checkout with the resort if your departure flight allows. Arrange a private luxury transfer to the airport in advance for a seamless departure.
